newsitem.title: UK: British firms most competitive in labour costs - survey.
newsitem.headline: British firms most competitive in labour costs - survey.

text.p: British firms are the most competitive in Europe in terms of labour costs, but at the expense of managers working longer hours and taking shorter holidays, a 3i European Enterprise Centre report said on Monday.

"Britain leads Continental Europe in labour competitiveness, but while they may have the lowest additional employment costs, the British work the longest hours and get the shortest holidays," the report said.

The survey of 490 small and medium sized enterprises in Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Spain, showed 55 percent of British companies estimated their additional labour costs, including social security, taxes and pension payments, to be less than 21 percent of overall outgoings, a stark contrast to France and Germany.
Nearly 40 percent of German firms said their additional labour costs were over 60 percent of their total wages.

As a result, British firms are more confident about their competitivenss. Fifty percent of British firms thought they were competitive, compared with just four percent of German companies, the report said.
But the survey showed that workers in each of the five countries worked longer hours than they were contracted for, with the British putting in the longest hours.
Forty-seven percent of Britons work over 40 hours a week, well above the 35 hour working-week which France's new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin hopes to introduce.

"It remains to be seen if the introduction of the Social Chapter and minimum wage legislation in Britain will impact significantly on the ability of British firms to maintain their competitive edge," said 3i marketing director Adam Quarry.
British and German firms said they were strongly opposed to the Social Chapter in principle, while 76 percent of French managers strongly supported it.
The 3i European Enterprise Centre was set up in 1990 to publish special reports on small and medium sized firms. It is funded by 3i, the UK provider of equity capital to private companies.
